sections.title: Letter A sound
paragraphs: The letter name is (A) /eɪ/. Its main sound is heard in (apple) /æ.pəl/, which is a round fruit. This letter makes four different sounds in English words.

sections.title: How to say letter A
paragraphs: For the first sound, drop your jaw low and spread your lips wide. Keep your tongue flat and push the front up a little. For the second sound, start with mid lips and glide smoothly upward. For the third sound, relax your whole mouth completely. For the fourth sound, open your mouth wide and pull your tongue back. Feel your throat vibrate with your voice for all four sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules for letter A
paragraphs: In closed syllables, it makes the sound heard in (cat) /kæt/. In open syllables or before a silent e, it sounds like (make) /meɪk/. In unstressed syllables, it becomes a weak schwa, as heard in (about) /ə.baʊt/. Before the letter r or in certain broad words, it makes the open sound heard in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with letter A
paragraphs: Learners often confuse the sound in (cat) /kæt/ with the sound in (father) /fɑː.ðər/. To avoid this error, open your mouth wider and push your tongue forward for (bag) /bæɡ/. Another mistake is making (baby) /beɪ.bi/ into one flat sound. Glide your tongue upward from the first sound to the second instead. Finally, never stress the weak ending in (sofa) /soʊ.fə/.
